accountDeletion.metaDescription: How to request deletion of your OnScreen account and associated data.
accountDeletion.title: Account & Data Deletion
accountDeletion.intro: OnScreen is a self-hosted media server. Where your account data lives — and how to delete it — depends on which OnScreen server you're using.
accountDeletion.selfHostedHeading: If you're using a server you run yourself
accountDeletion.selfHostedData: Your account and all associated data (watch history, favorites, profiles) are stored on the OnScreen server you or your server admin operates. The OnScreen project (the developers of the app and server software) does not have access to that data.
accountDeletion.selfHostedAsk: Ask the server's admin user to delete your account via {path} in the admin panel. The admin can remove your user record, watch history, favorites, profiles, sessions, and pairing tokens from their server.
accountDeletion.hostedHeading: If you have an account on a server the OnScreen developer runs
accountDeletion.hostedHow: This includes {site}. To delete an account on one of these servers, email {email} with the username (and, if known, the email address) of the account to delete.
accountDeletion.hostedTiming: We'll confirm receipt within 7 days and complete the deletion within 30 days. We may ask you to verify ownership of the account before deleting (for example, by responding from the email address registered with the account).
accountDeletion.deletedIntro: When your account is deleted, the following are removed from the OnScreen server:
accountDeletion.deletedUser: Your user record (username, email if provided, password hash)
accountDeletion.deletedProfiles: Managed profiles attached to your account
accountDeletion.deletedSessions: Active sessions, refresh tokens, and pairing tokens
accountDeletion.keptIntro: The following are {not} deleted because they aren't tied to your account:
accountDeletion.keptMedia: Media files in the library (these belong to the server's owner, not to individual users)
accountDeletion.keptAggregates: Aggregate analytics that have been stripped of user identity (e.g., total play counts per item) — your contribution to these cannot be reverse-attributed to you after deletion
accountDeletion.localHeading: Local data on your TV or device
accountDeletion.localIntro: The OnScreen TV app and other clients store the following on the device:
accountDeletion.localTokens: Authentication tokens (cleared when you sign out)
accountDeletion.localImageCache: An image cache (poster and thumbnail images downloaded for performance)
accountDeletion.localRemove: To remove all local data from a device, uninstall the app (Settings → Apps → OnScreen → Uninstall on Android TV / Google TV / Fire TV). All local data is wiped as part of the uninstall.
accountDeletion.retention: Deleted accounts are removed from the live database immediately. Database backups, retained for up to 30 days for disaster recovery, are overwritten on rotation; deleted accounts are not restored from backup.
accountDeletion.contact: Questions: {email} or open an issue at {issues}.

account.title: Account
account.statsDesc: Your own viewing and listening numbers: hours, top titles, genres, when you play, and your year in review. Only you can see them.
account.digestDesc: A weekly or monthly email of what was added to your libraries, with what you're in the middle of and your numbers for the period.
account.qualityDesc: Limits for your account on every device, at home and away; the server converts anything above them. The audio limit applies whenever audio is converted, and to music in apps that check with the server before playing. The web music player plays the original files.
account.languagesDesc: Audio and subtitle languages the player picks when a title has them, on every device you sign in to.
account.scrobblingDesc: Send what you play to ListenBrainz, Last.fm or Trakt.
account.passwordDesc: Changing it signs you out on your other devices; this browser stays signed in.
account.noPassword: You sign in through your organisation's sign-in or a profile, so there's no OnScreen password to change here.
account.devicesDesc: Browsers and apps signed in to your account. Signing one out ends its session at once; your other devices stay signed in.
account.revokeAllConfirm: Sign out every other device signed in to your account? This browser stays signed in.
account.downloadsDesc: Smaller copies you asked for from a title's Download menu. Each is kept for a while after you last downloaded it, then removed to save space.
account.apiKeysDesc: Long-lived keys for scripts and integrations such as Home Assistant or Kometa. A key can do what you can, except sign in or change your account's security. Revoking one stops it at once.
account.opdsTitle: Read your books in an e-reader app
account.opdsDesc: Apps such as KOReader, Moon+ Reader, Panels and Chunky can browse and download your book libraries over OPDS. Add this catalog in the app, create a read-only key above, and enter the key as the password (any user name).
account.opdsOff: Downloads are turned off on this server, so the catalog is unavailable until an admin turns them on.
account.dataDesc: Download a ZIP of what this server keeps about your account: profile and preferences, watch history and progress, ratings, favorites, playlists, reading positions, requests and signed-in devices. Passwords, two-factor secrets and keys are never included.
account.scrobble.timedOut: The {service} approval wasn't finished in time. Connect again to retry.
account.scrobble.title: Scrobbling
account.scrobble.lbDesc: When you finish a music track, OnScreen submits a listen to your {link} account. A play counts once you're past half the track, or four minutes — whichever comes first. One-way and best-effort: it never reads anything back and never affects playback.
account.scrobble.lbActive: Your ListenBrainz account is linked and listens are being submitted.
account.scrobble.lbPaused: A token is linked but scrobbling is currently off. Replace the token to re-enable it.
account.scrobble.tokenHint: Your token is stored encrypted and is never shown again. Unlinking removes it.
account.scrobble.lastfmDesc: Finished tracks are scrobbled to your {link} profile — same rule as above, half the track or four minutes — and the track you're playing shows as scrobbling now.
account.scrobble.lastfmDisconnectHint: Disconnecting forgets the link here. To revoke OnScreen's access on Last.fm too, remove it under Settings › Applications on last.fm.
account.scrobble.lastfmUnavailable: Last.fm isn't set up on this server yet: an admin adds a Last.fm API account in Settings.
account.scrobble.lastfmStep1: {link} and allow OnScreen access to your account.
account.scrobble.lastfmStep2: Come back here. This page finishes linking on its own.
account.scrobble.traktDesc: Movies and episodes you watch are scrobbled to your {link} history: a play that reaches 80% counts as watched, and a paused one keeps its progress there. While something plays, your profile shows it. Marking a movie, episode, season or show watched adds it to your history too.
account.scrobble.traktDisconnectHint: Disconnecting also revokes OnScreen's access on Trakt.
account.scrobble.traktUnavailable: Trakt isn't set up on this server yet: an admin adds a Trakt API app in Settings.
account.scrobble.traktStep: On any device, go to {url} and enter this code:
